projects.goal: Prepare Northwind's breach-of-contract position on the late and partly defective delivery under PO-4471: a chronology grounded in the documents, a brief whose factual assertions and quotations are checked against sources, and a rehearsal of the likely counterarguments.

intakeQuestions.question: Which document governs the delivery date: the master supply agreement or the purchase order?
intakeQuestions.answer: Both: MSA clause 7.2 makes PO delivery dates binding, and PO-4471 states 1 March 2026 and says time is of the essence.

intakeQuestions.question: Did Northwind use or resell any of the delivered units before rejecting?
Is the February email thread privileged?
intakeQuestions.assumption: Treated as not privileged (correspondence between the parties). Privilege review is pending the document-handling integration.

projects.summary: Northwind Supply (fictional) ordered 400 fabricated steel frames from Harbor Fabrication (fictional) under PO-4471 with delivery due 1 March 2026. Delivery arrived on 10 March with coating defects on 12 units, and Northwind rejected the lot on 12 March. A deterministic fact check found the draft brief asserting delivery on 3 March, contradicting the signed receipt; a quotation check found a misquoted sample authority; a contrary-authority search surfaced a fictional waiver case. A revised argument was approved by the responsible lawyer, brief v2 was imported, and the checks now pass. The rehearsal panel lists counterarguments to prepare for; it predicts nothing.

chronology.title: Master supply agreement signed
chronology.detail: Clause 7.2: PO delivery dates are binding; time is of the essence only where the PO expressly says so. Clause 9.1: buyer may reject non-conforming goods within 5 business days of delivery.

chronology.detail: 400 fabricated steel frames, delivery by 1 March 2026, 'time is of the essence'.

chronology.detail: Northwind replies that delivery is required by 1 March per PO-4471.

chronology.title: Delivery received
chronology.detail: Delivered 10 March 2026 at 14:20; receipt notes coating defects on 12 of 400 units.

chronology.title: Northwind rejects the lot

argumentMap.text: Harbor breached PO-4471 by delivering after 1 March 2026, a date that was of the essence.
PO-4471 required delivery by 1 March 2026 and states that time is of the essence.

argumentMap.note: Brief v1 said 3 March; corrected in v2 after the fact check.

argumentMap.text: Example Co. v. Sample Corp. (fictional authority): time is of the essence where the contract expressly so provides.
argumentMap.note: Brief v1 quoted it as 'in all commercial deliveries'; corrected in v2.

argumentMap.text: Northwind validly rejected the lot under MSA clause 9.1 within five business days of delivery.
Northwind sent its written rejection on 12 March 2026, two business days after delivery.
The receipt records coating defects on 12 of 400 units at delivery.
Model Builders v. Illustrative Materials (fictional authority): rejection within the contractual window is effective even where only part of the lot is non-conforming.
Northwind accepted the late delivery without reservation and so waived its right to reject (Placeholder Industries v. Specimen Logistics, fictional authority).
argumentMap.note: Surfaced by the contrary-authority search (model judgment). The lawyer has not yet decided how to address it.

argumentMap.text: Reservation was recorded on the receipt itself (coating defects noted) and the rejection followed within two business days.

rehearsal.disclaimer: Preparation exercise, not a prediction of the outcome.

items.text: Northwind accepted delivery on 10 March and signed the receipt, so it waived the right to reject.
items.preparedResponse: The receipt itself records the coating defects (DR-0931 p. 1 l. 9) and written rejection followed on 12 March, inside the five-business-day window of MSA clause 9.1.

items.text: 'Time is of the essence' appears only in the PO, not in the MSA, so it was never incorporated.
items.preparedResponse: MSA clause 7.2 makes PO delivery dates binding and provides for time-of-the-essence wording in a PO; PO-4471 contains it (p. 1 l. 6).

items.text: Only 12 of 400 units were defective; rejecting the whole lot is disproportionate.
items.preparedResponse: Rejection rests on lateness as well as defects; Model Builders (fictional) supports rejection of a lot that is partly non-conforming. Confirm whether any units were used (intake question iq-L2).

items.text: When exactly was the rejection notice sent, to whom, and how?
items.preparedResponse: Email of 12 March 2026 at 09:40 to Harbor's account manager (email thread p. 2 l. 4); a courier copy is referenced but not in the document set.

items.text: Did Northwind mitigate by sourcing frames elsewhere, and at what cost?
items.preparedResponse: Not in the document set. Open item for the client.
